newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 2.

text.p: Contradiction over Morgan's TV pay: A contradiction between comments by MP Tukoroirangi Morgan and Aotearoa Television Network financial records was detailed by TV1's Holmes programme last night. Page 1.
Police refer complaint to SFO: Police have referred a complaint from ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble alleging wrong-doing by NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan to the Serious Fraud Office. Page 1.
Cull decision outrages horse lovers: Conservation Minister Nick Smith has outraged horse enthusiasts with his announcement that 1200 Kaimanawa wild horses are to be culled from the herd. Page 2.

Peters forced to apologise to MP: Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters was forced to apologise on Thursday after accusing Labour MP Annette King of lying during a heated exchange in Parliament about his proposal for compulsory superannuation. Page 2.
Entry to House ironic, says MP: New MP Annabel Young said on Thursday it was ironic that she, an opponent of the introduction of MMP, entered the Parliament through MMP's list system. Page 2.

Peters should come clean say doctors: Senior public hospital doctors have called on Deputy Prime Minister Peters to come clean with his views on privatisation of public hospitals, as the Christchurch cardiac unit dispute drags on. Page 2.

Upton defends moth-spraying: Biosecurity Minister Simon Upton has rejected suggestions that the programme to rid Auckland's eastern suburbs of white-spotted tussock moth was doomed to failure. Page 3.

English won't say if he'll stand by letter: Health Minister Bill English on Thursday refused to say whether he would stand by his letter to Kaitaia pensioner Harry Findlay demanding that he pay $58,000 for his wife's hospital care. Page 11.

Governor provokes Kiwi's fall: The New Zealand dollar fell almost one-third of a United States cent on Thursday and interest rates eased slightly after comments by Reserve Bank governor Don Brash. age 13.

Tranz Rail warns earnings may fall: Tranz Rail has warned that earnings may fall in the June quarter after racking up a $20.6 million net profit for the March quarter, $6.2 million up on 1996's third quarter result. Page 13.
Telecom to spend millions on computer: Telecom will spend tens of millions of dollars in the next two years to avoid "Year 2000" computer problems. Page 13.
Radio Pacific buys seven northern stations for $3.5m: Radio Pacific has bought seven North Island radio stations from Radio Otago for $3.5 million. Page 13.
Ansett Australia wants to merge some operations with Air NZ: Ansett Australia is seeking to merge some of tis operations with its part-owner Air New Zealand. Page 13.

Audit Office to review Tradenz probe: The government's financial watchdog, the Audit Office, would review a Tradenz internal investigation into allegations of fraud by two staff members, Tradenz chief executive Fran Wilde said on Thursday. Page 13.

Resolute posts half-year profit: Mining company Resolute posted a net profit for the half-year to March of A$15.05 after it was hit by bad weather, changing contractors and lower-than-expected mine grades in the March quarter. Page 13.
